GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2011-03-13T19:28:07Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Mesh Load fails with texture-less model
Description: I have an OBJ model converted to JS with the python script, and it has no textures (only material colors). Here's one of the materials:

{
    "a_dbg_color" : 0xeeee00,
    "a_dbg_index" : 4,
    "a_dbg_name" : "skin",
    "col_ambient" : [1.0, 1.0, 1.0],
    "col_diffuse" : [1.0, 0.6139393939393939, 0.48],
    "col_specular" : [1.0, 1.0, 1.0],
    "illumination" : 2,
    "specular_coef" : 100.0,
    "transparency" : 1.0
}

Naturally, there are no UV coordinates in the model. Trying to load this gets the following error:

"Cannot read property 'length' of undefined". Here's the stack trace in Chrome:

Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'length' of undefined
d.h     Three.js:378
d        Three.js:379
THREE.Loader.createModel        Three.js:380
c.onmessage      Three.js:362

llm_response:
CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue is about a bug in the Three.js library where loading a mesh without textures causes an error. The problem is clearly identified as the code trying to access the length property of an undefined variable when loading an OBJ model that has no textures (only material colors). This is a conceptual issue that can be analyzed without needing to build or run the code. The error message and stack trace provide enough information to understand what's happening - the loader is expecting texture coordinates to exist but fails to handle the case when they don't. A solution would likely involve adding a check for undefined texture coordinates before trying to access their length. This type of issue can be verified through code analysis without needing to set up a build environment.
